quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: When should you conduct a safety inspection of your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen, avoid hazards and wind blasts, and stay out of other drivers' blind spots. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If hazards are on your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space from hazards. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: Which is not a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to danger.
It prevents you from finding an escape route.
It gives you room to steer your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles helps you respond if they make a mistake. It also gives you room to safely steer your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for the best grip.

questions.question: As your motorcycle accelerates, you will need to:
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle accelerates, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.
Other vehicles will enter the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let all other traffic and pedestrians go, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops. You can still control a locked rear wheel if the bike is upright and going straight.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash. They keep you comfortable and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the front brake immediately and then press it firmly again. Use both brakes together when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches your brain within minutes of drinking it and affects your riding ability right away. Riding while drunk is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: To be seen more easily by other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Wearing bright colors makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can make your motorcycle tip over.

questions.question: To be seen better by other drivers, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in bad visibility.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to ride with your headlight on all the time.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind.

questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a following distance of at least:
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep a following distance of at least three seconds when riding at night.

questions.question: The human body removes alcohol at a rate of:
questions.explanation: On average, the body removes alcohol at a rate of about one drink per hour. This varies by person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Position your motorcycle where other drivers can see you clearly when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn carts.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up.
The same time to stop and speed up.
More time to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows a motorcycle's acceleration and stopping. Your bike responds more slowly with a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good quality, properly fitted helmet is the best way to improve your survival chances in a crash.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift to a lower gear right away.
Ride in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on uneven bridge gratings, stay calm and go straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with its lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and proceed carefully. Always slow down and be ready to stop at an emergency scene.
